subject: RetailNova evaluation: throughput proof & renewal uptake path
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@retailnova.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@retailnova.com>, Derek Liu <derek.liu@retailnova.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Side-by-side evaluation: throughput proof request + renewal timeline

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As we discussed, RetailNova is running a narrow bakeoff between Redwood and AtlasAI ahead of our Feb renewal. The core ask from engineering is a short, reproducible throughput/latency benchmark for our typical payloads (avg prompt ~220 tokens, 8k context in some flows).

Concretely we'd like:
- a test harness or script we can run against a locked model endpoint (or instructions to reproduce on our side)
- p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec for steady-state traffic (10 concurrent sessions, 90% short-turn and 10% long context)
- sample logs and failure mode notes (e.g., memory pressure, spikes)

Procurement also asked for a clear path on pricing if we move to a Dedicated pool (expected uplift request: additional GPUs for peak weekends). Our renewal evaluation will weigh both performance and total cost of ownership.

Can you commit to a short benchmark run this month? If we have results by Dec 21 we can align legal and procurement for a Jan term sheet.

Best,
Elena
Elena Soto
VP Engineering, RetailNova
[Attachment: product-usage-summary.csv]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@retailnova.com>
Cc: Derek Liu <derek.liu@retailnova.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Side-by-side evaluation: throughput proof request + renewal timeline

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely run a focused throughput validation and share artifacts that map directly to your traffic profile. Proposed plan:
1) We provide a test harness and a small dataset you can run locally (or we can run from a dedicated Redwood bucket against a locked endpoint).
2) Redwood runs a dedicated perf run targeting your workload shape (10 conc., mixed short/long) and returns p50/p95 tokens/sec, memory traces, and a short ops-runbook describing mitigation options.
3) Post-run we’ll propose Dedicated sizing options and a phased pricing uplift (pilot credits -> committed pool discount).

Can you confirm whether you prefer: (A) we run against internal Redwood infra and share logs, or (B) you run the harness and send results? Option A gets you the fastest turnaround.

I’ll loop in engineering and security for SOC2/data retention clarifications. I’ve attached a tiny CSV template so your team can share sample payload mix if that helps.

- Kim
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-bench-template.csv]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 11:24:00 -08:00
Subject: FW: RetailNova evaluation: throughput proof request + renewal timeline

Folks — forwarding RetailNova (RN-5821). They want a short throughput proof this month, target results by Dec 21 if possible. Key asks: p50/p95 tokens/sec for mixed 10-concurrent sessions and failure mode notes.

Please advise:
- Marcus: can we allocate a dedicated perf run (fp16/quantized variant) and a small log export? Estimated runtime ~2-3 hours but needs GPU reservation.
- Neha: we need SOC2/data retention blurb and confirmation we can share sanitized logs (no PII).
- Priyom: pricing uplift for Dedicated pool (rough range, and pilot credit structure to propose).

Customer prefers Redwood-run (fastest). If we can commit to run by Dec 18–20 window we can meet their internal procurement timeline.

Thanks — Kim

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FW: RetailNova evaluation: throughput proof request + renewal timeline

Kim / Neha —

We can stand up a 4xA100 equivalent dedicated pool for a 3-hour perf window. Recommended config: fp16 with 8-bit quantization path (we'll test both fp16 and q4), sequence length profile to match their 8k flows. Ops notes:
- Warm KV cache for long-context sessions will improve steady-state throughput; cold-start spikes possible for first few long-context requests.
- Memory pressure may appear on >12 concurrent long-context sessions; we'll capture memory traces and throttling events.

I’ll prepare a step-by-step runbook and a short md with commands + expected artifacts. I attached the run plan.

- Marcus
[Attachment: marcus-benchmark-plan.md]

On Tue, Dec 14, 2027 at 11:24 AM kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Folks — forwarding RetailNova (RN-5821). They want a short throughput proof this month...

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 08:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FW: RetailNova evaluation: throughput proof request + renewal timeline

Kim / Marcus —

We can share sanitized operational logs and a SOC2 summary. Quick notes for procurement:
- We will redact any customer-provided PII fields before sharing logs; retention window for the perf artifacts will be 90 days unless RetailNova requests longer.
- SOC2 Type II summary and our control matrix (high level) can be provided under NDA. See attached short summary.
- Audit logs: we can export token-level usage for the perf window with hashed identifiers.

I will join the perf window remotely to confirm data handling.

- Neha
[Attachment: SOC2_summary.pdf]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@retailnova.com>
Cc: Derek Liu <derek.liu@retailnova.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Dec 2027 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Side-by-side evaluation: throughput proof request + renewal timeline

Elena —

Thanks — we’ve scheduled Redwood-run perf slots on Dec 20 and Dec 21. Plan attached and outlined below:

What we will deliver:
- Full perf run (Dec 20 09:00–12:00 PST) on a 4xA100-equivalent dedicated pool; we’ll test both fp16 and q4 variants.
- p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec, memory traces, KV cache hit rates, and a short ops-runbook outlining observed failure modes and mitigation steps.
- Sanitized logs and SOC2 summary (redacted PII) post-run.

Commercial path:
- Pilot: 2-week pilot with a 20% pilot credit (applied to first invoice) to validate production traffic.
- If you move to Dedicated: we propose a phased committed pool discount (15% on baseline committed spend) and options to burst additional capacity for weekends. Priyom will follow up with a draft term sheet and a modelled TCO comparison (inc. cost/token and expected uplift for the Dedicated pool).

Related links and artifacts: hubspot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/5821) and the harness we’ll use: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/retailnova-bench-harness

Attachments: test-harness-access.txt (access credentials + run steps).

Next steps: if this schedule works I’ll send calendar invites and a short pre-run checklist for RetailNova. Looking forward to the run — we’ll use the results to build a targeted upsell/renewal package.

Best,
Kim
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: test-harness-access.txt]
